records.summary: Article 11 of Timor-Leste's Petroleum Fund Law (Law No. 9/2005 of 3 August, republished with amendments by Law No. 12/2011 of 28 September) puts the Petroleum Fund in government hands and leaves the central bank executing. Article 11(1) says the Government is responsible for the overall management of the Fund. Article 11(2) says the Minister of Finance takes the decisions on the Fund's investment strategy and management, after first seeking the opinion of the Investment Advisory Board under Article 16. Article 11(3) says the Minister signs a contract with the Central Bank (in the 2011 text, with the 'Operational Manager', defined in Article 2(i) as the Central Bank) for the operational management of the Fund, and that the manager is answerable to the Government for that management. Article 16(1)(b) has the Advisory Board advise the Minister on the investment instructions the Minister gives the Fund's investment managers, and Article 2(h) counts the Operational Manager itself as an investment manager, so the instructions run to the bank. Article 12(5) requires the investment manager to act within any instructions issued by the Minister and within the operational management contract. The law is still the one in force in this version: Ministerial Diploma No. 4/2019 of 1 March 2019, published in the Jornal da Republica, cites Law No. 9/2005 'na redacao dada pela Lei n.o 12/2011' and names the Fund's Operational Manager as the Banco Central de Timor-Leste. The arrangement covers the Petroleum Fund only; the law says nothing about who sets interest rates or monetary policy.
records.source_title: Lei n.o 9/2005, de 3 de Agosto - Lei do Fundo Petrolifero, Jornal da Republica (Ministerio da Justica official journal)
records.quote: Artigo 11.o - Gestao do Fundo Petrolifero. 1. O Governo e responsavel pela gestao global do Fundo Petrolifero. 2. O Ministro nao tomara quaisquer decisoes relativas a estrategia de investimento e a gestao do Fundo Petrolifero sem primeiro obter o parecer do Comite de Assessoria para o Investimento nos termos do artigo 16.o. 3. O Ministro celebrara um contrato com o Banco Central para efeitos da gestao operacional do Fundo Petrolifero e o Banco Central sera responsavel pela gestao operacional do Fundo Petrolifero. [...] Artigo 12.o, n.o 5: O dever do Gestor de Investimento e maximizar o retorno dos investimentos do Fundo Petrolifero [...] em quaisquer instrucoes emitidas pelo Ministro e no contrato para gestao operacional referido no n.o 3 do artigo 11.o.

records.summary: In January 2025 a group of members of the Assembly of North Macedonia tabled a bill to amend the Law on the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia under the shortened procedure. Article 2 of the bill rewrites Article 15 of that Law so that, within four months of the end of the financial year, the National Bank Council distributes the financial result as follows: 30 per cent to general reserves until the level of base capital under Article 12(1) is reached, then 15 per cent after that level is reached, 'and 2) the remainder to the Budget of the Republic of North Macedonia', and adds that the Bank's income may be distributed only in that way. Article 1 deletes special reserves from Article 13(1) and deletes Article 13(4) altogether. Article 3 deletes point 9-a) from the National Bank Council's powers in Article 47(1). Article 4 orders the Bank to transfer the special reserves it had formed under the old Article 13(4), an amount the bill's explanatory part puts at almost 27 million euro, to the general reserves account within 30 days of the law coming into force, and bars the Bank from using those special reserves in the meantime. The bill's own reasoning says the aim is to raise the Bank's general reserves from 11 to 39 million euro. An amendment to that Law was in fact enacted and published as Sluzben vesnik 16/25: the National Bank's own regulatory decisions of 4 February 2025 and later cite the Law with its amendment list ending '110/21, 74/24 and 16/25', so 16/25 was in force by early February 2025, which fits a bill tabled that January under the shortened procedure. This is still filed as an attempt rather than a law change because the enacted text itself could not be read, so nothing here asserts that the bill's provisions are what 16/25 contains: the National Bank's own website names its current law file 'Zakon za Narodnata banka 16-25', which is consistent with publication in Sluzben vesnik 16/25, but that file and the Bank's whole site answer 403 to automated requests and the enactment could not be read.
records.source_title: Predlog na zakon za izmenuvanje na Zakonot za Narodnata banka na Republika Severna Makedonija, po skratena postapka, Skopje, januari 2025 (proposers: group of MPs)

Членот 15 се менува и гласи: „(1) Во рок од четири месеци по завршувањето на финансиската година, Советот на Народната банка го распределува финансискиот резултат за распределба на следниов начин: 1) 30% во општите резерви до постигнување на нивото на основниот капитал од членот 12 став (1) од овој закон, односно 15% по достигнување на нивото на основниот капитал од членот 12 став (1) од овој закон, а 2) остатокот во Буџетот на Република Северна Македонија. (2) Распределба на приходите на Народната банка може да се врши само на начин утврден во ставот (1) на овој член. [...] Член 4. (1) Износот на специјални резерви формирани согласно член 13 став (4) од Законот за Народната банка [...] се пренесува на сметката на општи резерви во рок од 30 дена од денот на влегувањето во сила на овој закон. (2) Во рокот утврден во ставот (1) на овој член, Народната банка не може да ги користи специјалните резерви.
